Build the compact identity tables

Source: R/md-compact.R
md_build_compact.Rd

Collapses name to one row per (ein, name_key) and address to one row per (ein, street_key, city_key, state, zip5) after domination pruning. Every contributing raw row is untouched — this is a derived layer beside md_build_derived()'s name_derived/address_derived, not a replacement. See dev/COMPACTION.md for the process this implements and what it measured against the real database.

Usage

md_build_compact(con = NULL, what = c("name", "address"), drop_guarded = TRUE)

Arguments

con

A connection from md_db().

what

Which compact tables to build.

drop_guarded

Leave out observed names flagged by md_guard_observed() and the addresses paired with them. Defaults to TRUE; a database where the guards never ran has no flags and loses nothing.

Value

Row counts, invisibly.

Why DROP-and-rebuild rather than update in place

If the ranking rule changes, the correct response is DROP TABLE and rebuild, the same posture md_build_derived() takes toward normalizer drift (section 9) — never an in-place reconciliation against tables meant to stay append-only.

Guarded observed rows

md_guard_observed() flags observed names written for the wrong EIN (name.guard_any). By default those rows, and the observed addresses paired with them through name_id, are left out before collapsing. A key also backed by an unflagged row (the BMF legal name, say) survives, carried by that row alone; a key backed only by flagged rows disappears. Raw rows in name and address are untouched either way.

With drop_guarded = FALSE every row is kept, and guard_any on the compact row is TRUE only when every row behind it was flagged, so a spec can still filter on it. In both modes the column exists, so the table's shape does not depend on the option.
